title: Quota edgecase lab notes — Jan 10 2028
content:
Purpose:
Quick lab notes and action items from the midweek session focused on quota edgecases affecting mixed routing/auth paths. This is an operational dump — raw observations, scratch math, and immediate follow-ups. Not a final postmortem.

Attendees (in order introduced): Dana, Marcello, Anya, Rohit, Priya, Alex (brief), SRE on-call (shadowed).

Context / why this matters:
- We observed intermittent "quota drift" where clients reported 403s while dashboard counters showed available tokens. Suspected race between decrement and route-level fallback.
- Several customers on Dedicated hit this during regional failovers last week; surface risk for reserved capacity QoS and billing reconciliation.

What we tested today (high level):
1) Simulated split brain of route-decider v2 -> v3 during canary rollout.
   - traffic generator: small bursts (500 qps) with mixed embedding/text requests, user-ids randomized, TTL for prefix cache set to 2s and 15s variants.
   - observed: when route-decider returned inconsistent route set, quota checks ran on stale controller (v2) and permitted the request; downstream v3 enforcement flagged as over-quota and returned 429/403 depending on fast-fail config.

2) Auth token rotation storm test (edge timing):
   - rotated signing keys every 7s in test harness, simulated 1000 concurrent short-lived streams (100–500 tokens each).
   - observed: 0.6% of streams hit transient auth failures and retried; when retry jitter was small (<50ms) the retry window aligned with quota decrement leading to double-counts in the metrics pipeline.

3) Quota reconcilers with delayed kafka consumer (backpressure):
   - delayed reconciler consumer group by 4–8s to mimic consumer lag.
   - observed: dashboard counters lagged real-time usage by several seconds causing manual intervention triggers; in one run we saw a customer-facing 403 returned while dashboard still showed capacity.

Raw numbers / quick metrics (from today's runs):
- Test run A (route flake): 20k requests total over 60s; inconsistency windows ~1.2–2.3s; ~0.9% requests had mismatch (allowed then rejected).
- Test run B (token rotation): 10k streams over 120s; 61 auth transient fails -> 49 retried within 200ms -> 31 double-decrements observed by reconciler.
- Reconciler lag injection: consumer lag 6s average -> dashboard under-reported by median 5.2s.

Key hypotheses built from the session:
- Root cause is multi-factor: route-decider rollout + differing enforcement semantics + delayed reconciliation pipeline together create short windows where enforcement and billing diverge.
- Retry jitter defaults are too small for our short TTLs and fast rotation scenarios.
- The quota check path and enforcement path don't share a single strongly-consistent source of truth; race is possible when routing changes mid-flight.

Immediate mitigation options (fast, tactical):
- Soft-fail mode: when enforcement mismatch detected, prefer serving with an informational warning and increment a special "race" metric instead of hard 403. (low-risk toggle)
- Increase default retry jitter to 200–500ms for client SDKs and gateway proxies. (requires SDK/policy coordination)
- Pause route-decider canary rollouts for 24–48h on customers with Reserved/Dedicated until we ship stronger consistency.

Proposed engineering fixes (medium term):
1) Atomic quota token bundle: bundle quota check + local enforcement token in one rpc to route-decider, return single signed token that downstream enforcement accepts; reduces split decision windows. (ENG-4321)
2) Reconciler fast-path: if kafka consumer lag > 2s, mark dashboard as provisional and emit real-time downstream counters for billing reconciliation. (Confluence draft linked)
3) Route-decider versioned contracts: explicit backwards-compatible enforcement semantics on minor versions — add compatibility tests to rollout pipeline.
4) Auth rotation coordination: on key rotation, add overlap window and require clients to accept tokens signed by previous key for an extra 1s by default.

Assigned action items (owner — ETA):
- Rohit: prototype atomic quota token bundle (spike) — EOD 2028-01-13; include perf baseline (tokens/ms) and simple threat model.
- Marcello: update client SDK jitter defaults; open PR for server-side proxy policy change to 250ms jitter — target 2028-01-17.
- Anya: add test case to rollout CI to simulate mixed-version route-decider and assert enforcement parity — 2028-01-15.
- Priya: draft incident postmortem template entries for quota-drift class and collect customer examples — 2028-01-14.
- Dana: coordinate with on-call to set temporary soft-fail feature flag in prod for affected customers — immediate (today) and validate metrics.

Open questions / risks to discuss next sync:
- Billing: if we soft-fail and serve, do we bill or credit? How do sales/legal want to handle customer disputes? (finance/legal loop required).
- SLA exposure: will this transient mismatch violate Dedicated SLOs? Need legal/CS input.
- Performance impact: atomic token bundle will add one extra RPC in happy path; need to measure 95th p99 impact under 2k–10k qps.

Notes from quick sync with SRE on-call:
- Add an alert for "enforcement-mismatch-rate" when > 0.2% over 5m, hit pager only if >1% for 15m.
- Instrument a tracing tag that carries route-decider version + enforcement-node-id to make debugging the short windows easier.

Scratch TODOs (not prioritized):
- Run test with TTLs at 50ms, 200ms, 2s to map sensitivity curve.
- Capture p99 latency per route-decider version with and without atomic bundle.
- Check whether HSM/KMS delays could amplify edgecases for auth rotation.

References / links pulled quickly:
- Linear: ENG-4321 (quota atomic bundle spike)
- Confluence: quota-edgecase-playbook (draft)
- Slack thread: #platform-ops pinned: "Jan9-dedicated-403s"

Final note / session summary (1 sentence):
Mixed timing between routing rollouts, auth rotations, and a lagged reconciliation pipeline is producing short windows of enforcement vs billing divergence — tactical guards and a medium-term atomic bundle design are the path forward.

Next sync: Mon 2028-01-16 10:30am PT (weekly follow-up) — agenda: Rohit spike results, SDK jitter PR, reconciler lag mitigation plan.

---
Conversation snippets (copied raw from the session):
"If route-decider v2 thinks user has 50 tokens and v3 thinks 0, downstream enforcement will always win if it checks later — the user sees a 403 even though the console says 50." — Marcello
"We should avoid treating the dashboard as source-of-truth in runbooks; it's eventual." — SRE on-call

End of notes.
